text: Look at us now
I said no to him once
She said no to me once
Now I can't stop looking
Now I can't stop them calling
I was so in love with her, I couldn't think straight
I asked her out at last, outside her front gate
Old hoodie, messy hair, a three-day beard
She looked at me the way I always feared
She said, I like you, but not like this
A man should take care of himself. That's it
I liked him, I swear it's true
But look at him, what could I do?
He didn't take care of himself
So how could he take care of me too?
Look at us now
I got home and stared at the mirror a while
Greasy hair, old hoodie, nothing worth a smile
So I started with the basics: barber, shave
Then every hoodie I owned went to the grave
I bought real clothes, the right size, for the first time
A navy knit, high collar, trousers that fit fine
I stood up straight; I never knew I was this tall
I walked out the door and the whole street felt small
I saw him on the street today
And I could not look away
Is that the boy I turned down?
He's the best-looking man in town
I want him, I want him now
I'll find a way somehow
Look at us now
I texted him last night
So did twenty girls last night
Look at us now
My phone used to be quiet, now it never stops
Girls I've never met are asking where I shop
One wants my number, one wants my name
One asks where the knit is from, so I tell her plain:
Moderno Milano. They all write it down
A year ago nobody looked at me in town
Then her name lights up my phone: hey stranger, drinks?
I read it twice, and I don't know what to think
A year ago I'd have run to her through the rain
Now I get to choose, so I don't run again
I was wrong about you then
You were right about me then
So can we start again?
I like you, I do. But I'm with someone now
I had him first, and I let him go
Now I'm the one hearing no
I told him to take care of himself
Now he takes care of someone else
I cry on the tram alone
He doesn't look at his phone
I was right, and I was late
Another girl is at his gate
I'm not angry. I'm not. I just moved on
You did. And now you're gone
And I'm the one who held on
Look at us now
Moderno Milano
